Hi Marissa,

We're seeing a sudden spike in 429 responses and sustained token-level latency from ~08:52–09:05 PT that is impacting our ingestion pipeline. Throughput dropped by ~45% and downstream jobs timed out. We've attached a small extract of the rate logs (orbit-rate-logs.csv).

Quick summary: 
- First 429s observed: 08:52:17 PT
- Peak 429 rate: 230/min between 08:56–08:59
- Median generation latency rose from ~120ms to ~1.2s
- Affects our prod ingest route: POST /v1/generate (api key: orbit-prod-01)

We are on a Reserved plan (dedicated-pool) and don't expect throttling at this level. Could you confirm whether anything changed to our rate limits or burst caps? We need immediate mitigation — either a temporary quota bump or whitelist for the next 2 hours while we stabilize.

Also: our SREs traced a few request ids (in the CSV) that consistently returned 429s. Please let us know next steps; this is blocking customer-facing pipelines.

Thanks,
Claire Zhu

Folks — quick update from runtime investigation. I pulled the account's active policy and traffic trace. Initial findings:

- Root cause: configuration divergence between the Dedicated pool rules and the account-level quota. Orbit's reserved capacity has a per-key burst window set to 60s but the cluster-level safety valve applies a 30s token-bucket refill during high-load reclaim. When two safety layers overlap we incorrectly compute the available burst and clients see 429s once both are consumed.
- Why it surfaced now: Orbit's recent batch job increased short-lived peak QPS; because the system aggregates across tokens and applies the cluster safety cap, that created a depletion event faster than the refill could replenish.
- Latency rise: because requests were requeued and then hit fallback slower paths (cold KV cache hits), observed per-request latency climbed to ~1s.

Proposed immediate mitigations (can be applied in <15 mins):
1) Emergency override: set account-level burst_window to 180s and increase burst_tokens by 2x for 2 hours.
2) Route Orbit's heavy POST /v1/generate traffic to the dedicated warm pool to avoid cross-account reclaim.
3) Short-term fallback: enable model-priority degradation (small model fallback) for non-critical jobs to reduce token-time.

If Sales signs off on an emergency quota increase, we can apply 1+2 now. Afterward we'll schedule a config fix: unify burst semantics so cluster and account levels use the same window and compute the aggregate token budget deterministically (INF-1832).

I included a small snippet of the policy diff and a log excerpt in the Jira ticket linked below.

-- Vivek

Subject: Orbit incident summary and request for exec approval (temporary quota + credit)

Team — looping in leadership because Orbit is an active trial customer with production pipelines and this incident risked SLA breach. Summary and ask below.

Summary:
- Impact: Orbit experienced 429 spikes and latency increases from 08:52–09:05 PT reducing ingestion throughput ~45%. They submitted logs and SRE trace; no data loss reported but downstream job delays caused customer impact.
- Root cause: burst policy misalignment between account-level settings and cluster safety valve. The two token-bucket windows collide under short-lived peaks and produce premature throttling.
- Mitigation applied: Vivek applied an emergency override (burst_window -> 180s, burst_tokens +2x) and routed heavy traffic to the dedicated warm pool at 12:05 PT; default behavior restored at 14:05 PT after traffic normalized. We also enabled model-priority degradation for background jobs.
- Action items: INF-1832 created to unify burst semantics and add an automated alert when account-level burst utilization crosses 70% of the aggregated safety budget.

Customer asks & commercial ask:
- Orbit requested a temporary quota bump during the incident window and one month of goodwill credits given impact to their production jobs.

Request to leadership (please reply with approval/rejection):
1) Approve temporary one-time credit: USD 8,000 (applied as account credit) — requested by Orbit.
2) Approve a temporary quota override while we finalize the config fix (already reverted after 2 hours).

If approved, I'll coordinate the credit and send a formal incident write-up to Orbit with timeline and preventive measures. Claire — we appreciate the quick escalation; we'll share a postmortem within 72 hours.

Attachments: slo-dashboard.png (customer-visible SLO chart)
